canal_p22_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_001.text: The cause hearing opened on the fifty-second morning beneath the grain-house awning. Rain had stopped, but drops still fell from its stitched edge whenever wind shook the roof. The gardener sat beside the reed household, with the stall owner keeping her own bundle of bills on her lap. Across the table, the quarry representative placed the permit copy under a flat stone. Yue recognized the stone as ordinary paperweight, not a charged tool. Pei asked everyone to move their cups away from the source pages before the first question became expensive.

canal_p22_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_002.text: The public drainage officer presented his actual upstream inspection. The private stock bank had narrowed the outlet below the permit's required clear width. He had reached the accessible point with the owner's permission and recorded its condition, not guessed it from a downstream cloud. The later correction restored the permitted space and had been accepted on his follow-up round. The quarry representative produced the paid private correction bill. Paying to remove the obstruction mattered; it did not erase the earlier narrowing or establish that no damage had resulted while it remained.

canal_p22_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_003.text: Yue's evidence concerned the lower canal. She laid out the dated reports, the isolation of the small upper pocket, the ground withdrawal, and the later measured fall. The report from above did not tell her the exact minute every private stock piece moved. A household's account of entering water did not locate every upstream cause. She answered the first question without embellishing her own role. Han listened from the public benches. When the clerk asked about the powered frame, Yue described its bounded accepted movement and the ordinary escape. Nobody at the table needed a lightning legend.

canal_p22_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_004.text: The gardener said water crossed his protected rows after the lower channel rose, and that the stock bank's slump made the rise last longer. He had watched from the higher path after withdrawing. The officer asked which parts he saw and which he inferred afterward. The man disliked the question, then separated them. He had seen the rows inundated and the water hold; he had learned about the narrowed outlet from the later report. Yue copied the distinction with his approval. His loss remained real when its explanation became less certain.

canal_p22_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_005.text: The quarry representative offered the day's rainfall totals from its own receiver. They showed heavy rain and could help explain the large flow; they did not excuse a permit breach by making the storm impressive. Pei compared their dates with the lower observer messages. One copied sheet named the following morning where its source named the previous evening. The representative accepted the correction after reading the original. He seemed surprised that an error could be fixed without the room immediately deciding he had forged the weather. Luo asked him to continue.

canal_p22_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_006.text: The reed household described moving to higher ground before the worst water and returning to find the roof damaged. Their accepted three-copper replacement price had already been paid under their private arrangement. Lost reed stock and a ruined mat remained additional harms. The hardship gift had helped them rebuild and eat; it contained no claim waiver. The quarry representative asked whether relief grain counted toward compensation. The receiver showed the separate food offer. Twelve delivered household sacks were a limited gift, not a price paid for the right to stop hearing about the storm.

canal_p22_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_007.text: The stall owner laid out spoiled ingredient quantities, the extra market carrying expense she had actually paid, and the later sales that reduced the loss. She left her nephew's voluntary help outside the expense sum. A man on the public bench asked whether all that could truly follow from a narrow outlet. She said she had not come to offer a complete water model. She wanted the room to know what happened to her food and work. Yue watched the man's expression change when a pot became a household instead of a conveniently small figure.

canal_p22_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_008.text: The quarry representative brought a letter authorizing a bounded contribution from current private quarry funds. Nine copper could be paid toward the three households' documented current losses, without pretending to purchase silence about every future claim. The proposed distribution was four to the gardener, three to the reed household, and two to the stall. Each would see the actual scope before choosing whether to accept. The money was not yet on the table. Pei recorded the offer as an offer and asked when the authorized cashier could actually deliver it.

canal_p22_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_009.text: The cashier was at the regular landing and could bring the nine copper that afternoon. The representative did not want the contribution described as an admission that his employer caused every storm loss. The households did not want acceptance described as a full settlement of every unanswered responsibility question. The officer proposed exact language: payment toward the recorded current loss items under this agreement, with the permit breach separately determined and broader unsupported claims neither granted nor waived. They read it together. Nobody called the clause beautiful; several people said it was usable.

canal_p22_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_010.text: The ordinary permit authority also required its two-copper penalty for the proved narrowing. That payment belonged to the authority's regular account and would be made separately by the quarry. It was not taken from the nine offered to households or the canal's repair allocation. The representative checked his authorization and confirmed the cashier had a separate sum. Yue placed a blank space for the actual receipt reference. A penalty that disappeared inside compensation would leave two promises relying on the same coins, however sternly the official read it aloud.

canal_p22_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_011.text: Luo wanted the public finding to say that the narrowed outlet had worsened the lower flood. The officer explained what his present evidence supported: it had restricted discharge during a large inflow and increased the risk and persistence of high water along the connected lower reach. Individual crop and building losses had other conditions as well. Yue could testify to lower timing and observed effects, not assign an exact share of every loss. Luo folded her arms. She was angry on the households' behalf and disliked being unable to turn that anger into a precise instrument.

canal_p22_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_012.text: At the break Tian brought tea from the stall owner at its ordinary private price, paid from the people ordering cups. The household relief sacks did not supply a free feast because the hearing was difficult. Han bought one cup and forgot where he put it. Luo moved it away from the permit before he remembered. The quarry representative asked Tian whether she was the seamstress who had made the emergency covers. She said yes, already paid under the materials order. Her completed work did not qualify her to answer questions about the entire upper storm.

canal_p22_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_013.text: Bao attended only the brief seated interval he had accepted. He confirmed the dated ordinary bracket observation and the wrist restriction that led to the emergency labor transfer. The road crew's actual hours were in their signed appointment sheets; their absence did not erase what had been paid and done. A spectator wanted to know whether Bao's injury proved the public rescue had been reckless. He described the private wet packing cloth and his level-ground slip, without making the answer decide every other movement that night. Then his sister took him home before the chair began to hurt.

canal_p22_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_014.text: Han gave the financial account only when asked about resources used during the storm. The relief and hardship funds remained separate from his public loan. The forty-eight conditional private deposit had been refunded from the actual thirty-two reserved and sixteen private sale receipts; listed private security was released. The valid public loan still stood at fifty-six after the twenty-four payment. He could not collect that balance by reviving completed household labor or selling the common bed. He said the words without embellishing how much they had cost him to accept.

canal_p22_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_015.text: The gardener asked whether future maintenance could be funded by requiring households to give one day every winter. The suggestion came from him, not from an old pledge. Tian asked what happened to a widow unable to do the work or a seamstress away on a paid trial. He said substitutes could pay. She asked who set the price and whether water access would depend on it. The room grew thoughtful rather than hostile. The idea needed current authority, terms, and actual consent; it could not arrive as the familiar old annex with a new winter heading.

canal_p22_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_016.text: The trustees' draft instead used collected toll receipts, current priced appointments, and voluntary contributions offered on stated terms. The twenty-eight households could name representatives for planning without promising every member's labor. Ordinary lawful water access followed the posted use rules, not whether a family supplied free hands. A new compulsory levy would require the actual authority and process beyond this commission, not a sentence Yue inserted because the gate needed help. The gardener disliked losing his tidy solution. He acknowledged that he had proposed it partly because he was tired of counting money.

canal_p22_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_017.text: The cabinet maker attended with the corrected return notice folded in his pocket. He asked whether the charter would prevent future tenants receiving maps that concealed a public route. The officer proposed a current boundary copy delivered with any permitted adjacent storage arrangement and an end date visible beside temporary occupation. The landlord did not object. His rent amendment belonged to the private file. Yue wrote the public notice requirement in plain terms. It could change a future decision at the shed door, which seemed a better purpose than making the charter sound eternal.

canal_p22_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_018.text: The old check worker asked for task notices to include actual hours and rates before workers traveled to apply. Pei's limited assistant would keep the board current within the funded post; two months did not purchase every winter errand. The private merchants' four-copper grant had actually been received apart from the toll division. After it ended, a continuation would need fresh money and acceptance. The worker approved the clause, though it did not promise him a job. Han's completed private inventory had paid two copper already. One honest small result could stand beside a larger unanswered need.

canal_p22_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_019.text: The young keeper proposed a service clause saying who received a call when Luo was away. She named the actual current alternate, not the nearest household whose window happened to be lit. The alternate had replied under his own accepted appointment. The future fixed four-copper keeper fee covered the short defined rounds; emergency watches and loaded repairs required fresh priced work. Luo listened without interrupting. The girl had stopped offering to do everything in order to be trusted. Yue felt proud of her, then remembered that the trust belonged first to the people who would work beside her.

canal_p22_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_020.text: Pei read the debt clause from the original term and current balance. Fifty-six copper remained valid under the eligible actual-receipts share. The proposed four-copper installments would take fourteen payable months, with high costs or closed traffic able to delay a payment lawfully. Han wanted a review when an installment was missed, so silence could not masquerade as a cost. The trustees accepted a dated account available to the creditor. The clause kept his claim visible while denying it a body made from descendants' labor. He signed the draft for further reading, not as a final charter yet.

canal_p22_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_021.text: The gardener went outside during the next break and stared at the mud along the grain-house wall. Yue joined only after he waved her over. He said four more copper would not restore the season. She agreed. He wanted her to say the quarry should pay all of it. Yue could explain the evidence and current offer, but she could not make a wish into a proved share. He kicked a small clod apart. "Then let the finding be useful enough to keep them from stacking there again." She promised only to ask the actual officer about enforcement.

canal_p22_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_022.text: The officer's answer was practical: current clear-width markers, routine permit inspections under his standing work, and required authorization before stock altered the outlet again. The quarry had funded its own correction and could be penalized for another proved breach. The canal would receive a current contact for observed upstream changes; its keeper would not become an unpaid inspector of every private bank. The gardener read the enforcement clause and accepted its limited use. The people in the room could still hold a business to an actual condition without pretending the world beyond that business had become safe.

canal_p22_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_023.text: Three parts of the afternoon still required close attention. The households would read the offered compensation scope before accepting actual coins. The charter's labor and debt clauses would receive a plain-language comparison with the old annex. The upstream evidence would be checked for what it established and what remained uncertain. Yue had one agreed hearing interval to spend among them. Each mattered to tomorrow's final findings. The others would continue with their actual clerks, representatives, and witnesses. Pei arranged the folders so nobody could accidentally sign a payment while thinking it was a weather receipt.

canal_p22_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_024.text: The cashier arrived carrying a small locked private box and two separate authorized sums. The nine household copper and the two permit penalty copper were counted apart before anyone signed a receiving line. The households were not asked to endorse the penalty in order to eat. The quarry representative read his employer's authority one last time and handed Pei its copy. A child standing under the awning asked why such small piles required so many adults. Tian replied that adults were particularly talented at making small piles disappear. The cashier looked offended until everyone laughed.

canal_p22_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_025.text: The draft charter used twenty-three current household representatives present and five accepted written replies or proxies for this reading. It did not claim twenty-eight bodies filled the room or every resident agreed with each sentence. Final approval would occur at closure after the posted review interval. Dissenting comments stayed beside the draft. Yue checked the current replies against actual names rather than old household heads. One representative's husband had signed the proxy with her permission and named it as such. Her own written amendment appeared in the margin where the table could see it.

canal_p22_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_026.text: Late light reached the edge of the awning and turned the wet hanging threads gold. Tian examined the old seam overhead and said somebody had stitched it while hurrying. Pei asked whether it would hold until tomorrow. Tian checked the loaded line and said the present arrangement was sound, but a dry future repair would make sense. She did not accept the work by mentioning it. The trustees added a request to the ordinary building list. Yue smiled at how useful a sentence could remain when nobody tried to turn it immediately into another person's unpaid evening.

canal_p22_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_027.text: The household copies of the contribution agreement lay ready on three separate boards. The charter comparison used a fourth board, with the four finished annual seasons and current priced tasks on facing pages. The upstream evidence lay under flat stones at the dry center table. Bao had gone, Jiang was not appointed to return, and no charged apparatus had appeared to make the dispute easier. Yue looked at the ordinary tools of the hearing. They could do less than command a gate, and in several ways they could keep a command from becoming the next mistake.

canal_p22_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_028.text: Luo asked Yue whether she wanted to take the quarry representative outside and make him see the gardener's drowned rows. He had already agreed to an ordinary accompanied viewing if the household wished it; Yue would not stage a punishment disguised as inspection. Luo nodded, then apologized for the suggestion. She was tired. Yue bought her tea from her own purse and told her to sit through one actual break. The young keeper would finish the appointed round. A keeper could care fiercely for households without carrying every grief on her feet.

canal_p22_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_029.text: Yue chose her afternoon interval from the three current tables: the actual household contribution, the charter comparison, or the bounded upstream findings. Each held a decision people could still change after reading what they were about to approve. Outside the awning the canal kept its ordinary level, unconcerned with phrases that claimed to settle it forever. The new map lay beside the old one, the cashier waited with actual coins, and Pei had a fresh broad pen ready. Yue went where she could help the next answer become clear enough to use.

choices.text: Read the households' contribution agreements before payment.
Compare the charter with the completed labor annex.
Check the bounded upstream findings and penalty receipt.

canal_p22_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_030.text: The gardener read the contribution agreement standing up, as if sitting might make acceptance too easy. Yue waited beside his chosen household witness. The four copper were a payment toward the current documented loss items, not the value of his whole season or a promise that no further supported question could be raised. He asked to add that sentence in ordinary words above his signature. Pei approved the clarification. The quarry representative read it and agreed. The gardener sat only after the change was copied onto both versions, making the table feel less like a place he had surrendered.

canal_p22_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_031.text: His household witness counted the actual four copper with the cashier and placed them in the gardener's own purse. The receiving date and agreement reference went beside the count. The earlier four-copper private hardship gift stayed in its separate record; it had never bought a waiver and was not secretly refunded. The gardener said he would use the new contribution for the next planting and household needs he chose. Yue wrote no instruction over his money. She could help him understand the agreement without becoming another person telling his land what it owed.

canal_p22_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_032.text: The reed household's roof bill showed an actual three-copper replacement, distinct from the ruined mat and lost stock. They accepted the new three-copper quarry contribution toward the current documented losses under the stated scope. The earlier hardship gift and household food sacks remained separate support. The cutter counted the coins aloud, then gave them to his wife to keep dry. He asked whether accepting meant they had to say the quarry representative was a good man. Yue said the document contained no such requirement. His wife looked pleased enough to agree with the document for that reason alone.

canal_p22_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_033.text: The stall owner checked her two-copper contribution against the chosen spoiled-stock items. She retained the reduced loss after private higher-market sales, and no charge for her nephew's voluntary help appeared. The actual two coins came from the same separate nine-copper quarry sum, completing its four-three-two distribution. She signed the bounded receiving line after reading it aloud. Then she asked the representative whether he wanted a paid ginger bowl. He accepted and paid its posted price from his own pocket. The transaction looked awkward and ordinary, which suited the owner more than a ceremonial handshake.

canal_p22_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_034.text: The three receipts conserved the nine copper exactly. No household was asked to return its food grain, the earlier hardship gift, or a private refund to make the quarry contribution look larger. Their agreements named current loss items and preserved unsupported broader questions as unresolved rather than automatically granted. Yue checked the copies against each receiving line. The gardener stopped her before she walked away. "I am still angry." "I know." "Write that only if I ask." She put the unused summary page back. Some answers belonged to the person saying them, not to the proof of her listening.

canal_p22_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_035.text: The quarry representative asked to accompany the gardener to the higher viewing point after the hearing. The man agreed, naming the safe path and refusing a walk through his damaged rows. Yue did not attend merely to watch him be humbled. The household's witness went, and the representative's ordinary work time covered the visit. They returned with no new claim that seeing mud had supplied exact causation. The representative wrote that the current loss was visible and serious. The gardener approved that limited sentence and declined the man's suggestion of a public photograph of the household.

canal_p22_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_036.text: The reed wife wanted the report to describe the roof repaired and stock still lost. Her husband preferred a sentence saying they had come home. They found room for both. Yue copied their chosen words and read them back, leaving private sleeping and provision details out. The contribution did not turn them into witnesses for every quarry defense. A paid roof could be sound while the season's income remained damaged. The cutter looked at the three new copper and said he might buy better ties next spring. His wife told him to price them before promising the roof another miracle.

canal_p22_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_037.text: The stall owner returned to her hearth before the hearing ended. She had chosen the receiving scope, received the money, and authorized her nephew to collect the final public summary. Remaining did not make her claim more deserving; leaving did not make her gratitude smaller. Yue carried the actual instruction to the clerk. The nephew arrived with an empty pot and asked whether any tea remained. Pei found a little, then insisted he move the pot away from the coins. Tian said the office had begun to distrust every container, which made even the cashier laugh.

canal_p22_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_038.text: The cashier closed the empty nine-copper compartment after all three receiving notes matched. Its authorized private contribution was complete. The separate two-copper permit penalty awaited the authority's own receipt and could not be marked paid merely because the household box was empty. Yue kept the two accounts on different covers. The representative thanked her for the clarity, and she accepted the thanks without making him an innocent man or a villain in the same breath. The officer would determine the permit breach from evidence; people at this table had determined how to receive actual support.

canal_p22_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_039.text: By the end of Yue's interval the household agreements were readable, the nine coins disbursed, and the chosen public descriptions approved. The gardener walked home with his witness. The reed household carried its copy in a dry wrapper. The stall's nephew left with the summary contact and a small paid bowl for his aunt. Yue went back beneath the awning feeling tired in a way no brief qi practice could improve. She drank ordinary water and waited for the other tables' reports. The work had changed what three households could afford tomorrow without claiming to restore yesterday.

canal_p22_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_040.text: The old labor annex lay on one board and the current charter draft on another. Tian read the first heading aloud: four annual maintenance seasons, including the founding emergency winter, sixty worker-days each. All two hundred forty had been accepted complete. Yue placed the current job sheet beside it. Twenty-eight ordinary equivalents and eight separately funded emergency equivalents were this commission's actual appointments. They did not renew the old pledge. The gardener's proposed winter day had been a new suggestion, not a discovered unpaid balance. A representative frowned, then asked to read the completed certificate himself.

canal_p22_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_041.text: The certificate's receiving references matched the archive findings and household corrections already recorded. Its collective completion did not erase Qiao Lan's repaired personal name or require Tian to prove her father's hours again. Han watched the comparison and admitted his copied annex had begun below the original limit. Yue let his acknowledgment remain specific. The current charter needed no clause declaring his family incapable of future dealings. It needed the actual boundary between a valid toll claim and labor that could not be revived. Tian put a broad line beneath the two separate headings.

canal_p22_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_042.text: A representative disliked the phrase "voluntary labor" because it had once meant everyone knew which households would be shamed for declining. Tian suggested "work offered and accepted on stated terms," with price and interval named where paid. Gifts could remain gifts, and declining one would not remove ordinary lawful water access. The chair accepted the change for the next reading. Yue wrote the old phrase beside the correction rather than pretending it had never been proposed. The representative who objected looked surprised to be useful after sounding so distrustful. Tian said distrust sometimes had excellent handwriting.

canal_p22_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_043.text: The water-use clause applied posted rules to households and lawful users. It gave no clerk permission to threaten a seamstress's boat access because she chose winter work elsewhere. Actual damage or unpaid posted charges could still receive their ordinary process. The separation prevented generosity becoming the hidden price of using common water. Luo asked who would stop a keeper from quietly reviving the old expectations. The trustees proposed current posted task notices, named receiving contacts, and the retained ability to question an unaccepted appointment. Luo nodded and asked them to include her own position among the people bound by it.

canal_p22_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_044.text: The debt balance remained fifty-six. Twenty-four had been paid from the initial available reserve, while ninety-six stayed with the repair allocation. Future eligible actual receipts could pay four per payable month after operating costs and reserve needs under the accepted terms. Fourteen payable months was a calculation, not a prophecy of fourteen open winters. Han requested a current account when costs delayed a payment. The clerk's post had actual limited funding, and the creditor could read the ordinary account through its receiving office after that. They did not promise a free private copy on every day he worried.

canal_p22_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_045.text: The private gear lease began after the fifty-sixth closure and paid four monthly for the defined service condition, with review and no ownership transfer. Han's crane, shed, platforms, and listed stores remained private. The common bed, marked path, and diversion use remained outside their title. Yue drew the crane's reduced accepted swing on the practical copy, stopping it clear of the public wall. A loader at the table recognized the restriction and asked whether the lease might tempt people to resume the wider old sweep. Luo wrote the actual reduced movement into the receiving condition beside the fee.

canal_p22_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_046.text: The keeper's fixed four monthly copper paid short defined rounds, not every possible emergency. The separately received four-copper merchant grant supported two months of limited record intervals at two per month. Neither fund bought the descendants of a current worker. Yue watched the assistant compare her own appointment with the proposed charter phrase. She asked to add an explicit end date on every short post. Pei accepted it immediately and then looked annoyed that she had not said it first. Their small rivalry seemed likely to keep future forms readable without asking either woman to become infinitely available.

canal_p22_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_047.text: The common return route appeared in the boundary copy with its damaged portion closed and the sound winter alternative shown. Temporary adjacent storage needed an actual current permission and visible end date. Private shed access did not become public merely because an officer once passed through under invitation. The cabinet maker read that sentence twice and approved it. Yue remembered the wax pot moved away from her boots and was glad the charter could preserve a courtesy without turning it into a permanent obligation. The landlord signed receipt of the practical notice and kept his private rent dispute separate.

canal_p22_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_048.text: When the chair read the amended draft, the twenty-three representatives present could respond in their own words. The five written replies or accepted proxies remained beside it. One household disliked the voluntary-work clause because it feared nobody would offer repairs. Another disliked the debt share because it feared Han would never release resentment. The draft did not pretend those fears vanished. Its answer was current paid tasks, finite reserves, and review of actual receipts. Final approval would wait until closure after the posted interval. Yue marked the disagreements for the next copy instead of describing the room as united.

canal_p22_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_049.text: Tian took the plain comparison to the public board after the clerk checked it. It showed old pledge completed, current jobs finite, valid debt bounded, and private gear distinct from common routes. Nobody would need to read the faded original to learn the immediate consequence. Yue helped hold the board while Tian tied it under the dry eave. A passerby asked if this meant the canal was free. Tian said it meant posted use charges and actual tasks remained, without an inherited back underneath them. The man read the next line and said the toll still seemed too high.

canal_p22_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_050.text: The drainage officer spread his source sketch beside the permit. The raised private stock bank had narrowed the required outlet width during the inspected condition. A later private correction restored the clear passage, accepted on follow-up. Yue placed the lower timing sheets nearby and asked which inference the officer would sign. He could support restriction of discharge and increased high-water risk and persistence along the connected reach. He would not assign an exact fraction of the storm to every field and roof. The quarry representative read the proposed finding and asked two precise questions rather than objecting to the weather.

canal_p22_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_051.text: One question concerned the time between the owner's first local warning and the canal's receipt of it. The dated dispatch and actual receiving note differed by the ordinary boat journey, not by a mysterious vanished day. Pei's corrected copy preserved both. Yue testified to when Luo's crew acted at the lower fork and where the household withdrawal had reached. She did not know what every upstream worker said in private. The officer kept the communication timing in the findings without making it a complete defense or an additional secret offense. A delay needed its actual cause before becoming someone's intention.

canal_p22_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_052.text: The second question concerned the old ridge slide that had changed the seasonal lower route before the storm. Yue presented the current downstream survey and the householder's inspection permission. The channel's new course helped explain which plots received flow; it did not authorize the quarry's stock bank to narrow the outlet. The public report kept both conditions. The gardener had wanted one cause he could point at from his door. Reading the comparison, he said it would be easier to speak about if the world had only one bad piece of ground. The officer agreed without changing the finding.

canal_p22_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_053.text: The quarry representative produced the private correction bill again and asked that its actual acceptance be included. The officer did so with the receiving date. A breach repaired after inspection was still a breach during the proved earlier condition, but future readers should know the outlet no longer had that obstruction. Yue checked the lower current notice so Luo would receive the same information. The keeper had no reason to keep acting on an old report once a competent current inspection replaced it. Correcting danger did not erase accountability, and accountability did not require preserving the danger.

canal_p22_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_054.text: The ordinary permit authority's receiver counted the separate two penalty copper and issued its own dated reference. That actual payment completed the penalty line under the current determination. It never entered the canal repair, hardship, grain, or household contribution accounts. The cashier kept the receipt with his employer's authority copy. Yue checked the number and wrote it in the blank left that morning. Eleven private quarry copper had now served two distinct purposes: nine toward three households' current documented losses and two to the permit authority. There was no remaining secret pile for tomorrow's promises.

canal_p22_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_055.text: A spectator claimed that the small powered frame must have drawn the storm toward the canal. Yue answered only the actual mechanism question: external charged stones supplied the bounded apparatus work; stormlight had not fueled it or altered her realm. The officer's flow finding rested on rain, outlet condition, route, and observed water, not a rumor of cultivation attracting clouds. Luo asked the spectator what he had actually seen. He had seen a flash upriver from his doorway. They recorded no invented connection. Tian offered him tea if he paid the same price as everyone else.

canal_p22_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_056.text: The officer invited any witness with a source the table had missed to submit it through the named receiver. That did not reopen every concluded money count or promise a finding in favor of whoever spoke loudest. The reed wife added a precise roof observation already reflected in her bill. A quarry worker corrected which day a stock marker had been moved. Pei kept the chosen statement beside its source and date. Yue appreciated the room's willingness to change a detail without treating the whole day as failed. The broad final finding would be read again tomorrow before receiving signatures.

canal_p22_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_057.text: Luo studied the draft after the others stepped away. Its language did not satisfy her appetite for justice, but its enforcement clause could keep the outlet clear and its current contact could carry warnings. She asked the officer to show the exact marked width to the quarry crew at the next routine inspection. He agreed within his standing appointment. Yue watched her anger become a useful request. She did not call that anger excessive. It had brought households into the room; the final report simply needed tools it could actually wield once their voices quieted.

canal_p22_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_058.text: The quarry representative accompanied the gardener's chosen viewing later that afternoon from the safe higher path. His acknowledgment of visible loss went into the household file only after the gardener approved the wording. It supplied no new measurement of exact causation. Back at the table he said he had underestimated the difference between a damaged plot and a financial entry. Yue kept the sentence out of the official finding. It belonged to a conversation unless he and its subject wished to publish it. The gardener's copied loss account already said enough for the current payment.

canal_p22_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_059.text: By evening the bounded findings showed the permit breach, accepted correction, actual penalty, connected high-water risk, and limits on assigning individual loss shares. The household contribution had its separate four-three-two receipts; the charter clauses still awaited final approval after review. Yue returned the source sketches to their actual holders and kept the approved copies with the commission folder. Nothing in the hearing advanced her cultivation. She had learned to hear more without commanding more. At the safe landing the ordinary canal made the same low sound it had made before anyone offered to explain it.

canal_p22_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_060.text: The hearing reconvened on the fifty-third morning with drier boards and more tired faces. Pei read the corrected dates first. The quarry representative, households, and public officer could then hear the findings without spending the first hour rediscovering yesterday's copying error. Yue stood at the lower-observation table during her named closing work interval. A gust lifted the awning edge and sent one drop into the cashier's empty box. Tian laughed that even the weather wanted a receiving note. The cashier put the box away before the joke acquired a quantity.

canal_p22_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_061.text: The final permit finding established the proved narrowing of the required outlet by the private stock bank. The competent officer's follow-up had accepted the privately funded correction. The separate two-copper penalty had actually reached the regular authority with its own receipt. The report supported restricted discharge and increased connected high-water risk and persistence during the relevant condition. It did not assign an exact share of every storm loss or invent a complete upper weather record. The representative accepted receipt of the finding while retaining the ordinary right to question it through the named authority.

canal_p22_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_062.text: The three households read their chosen current loss descriptions and contribution scopes. Nine actual private quarry copper had been delivered four to the gardener, three to the reed household, and two to the stall. These receipts did not refund or silently offset the earlier ten-copper private hardship gift, nor the twelve food sacks. Their agreements covered the specified current contribution, with unsupported broader questions unresolved rather than promised in their favor. Pei checked every copy with its receiver. The stall owner signed, then left to work before the tea stove began to steal another morning.

canal_p22_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_063.text: The garden household kept its drowned rows and future seed plan distinct. The reed household's roof was repaired while lost stock remained. The stall had reopened with smaller actual purchases. The hearing did not announce those lives restored because money had changed hands. It recorded what the households chose to say and what current payments could do. Yue carried the gardener's corrected copy outside when he asked. He looked at the four new coins in his own purse and said he would rather buy seed than make another speech. She wished him a useful season without predicting it.

canal_p22_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_064.text: The quarry's clear-width markers and future permit inspections belonged to the actual officer's standing work and the owner's compliance. Luo received the current upstream contact and accepted correction notice. She would report observed changes through that contact, not become an unpaid upper inspector. The canal's lower route and protected plots remained subject to their own current conditions. The separate enforcement record would survive the commission's closure. Yue checked its receiver before filing her copy. There was now a practical answer to the gardener's request to prevent the same stock arrangement returning after everyone forgot the wet night.

canal_p22_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_065.text: The draft charter went up for its final posted review before closure. Twenty-three representatives had participated in the reading, with five actual replies or accepted proxies beside it. Differences remained in the margin. The completed four annual seasons totaled two hundred forty accepted worker-days; no copied heading could revive them. Current work would be offered and accepted on stated terms. Ordinary lawful water use followed posted rules, not whether a household supplied free labor. Tian stood beside the plain comparison while people read it. She let the toll complaint remain a toll complaint instead of treating every objection as disloyalty.

canal_p22_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_066.text: The valid public debt stayed at fifty-six under the actual eligible-receipts term. Four copper per payable month made fourteen payable installments, with real operating costs and closed traffic able to delay one. The creditor would receive a current account when that happened. The future gear lease paid four monthly for the defined private service condition, beginning only after closure. The fixed keeper fee was another four for short defined rounds. The extra limited record post relied on its separate received four-copper grant for two months. Pei read the four different fours slowly until even Han stopped trying to combine them.

canal_p22_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_067.text: Han's private loading property stayed private, with the reduced accepted crane movement clear of the public wall. The common bed, marked paths, and diversion use stayed outside that title. His forty-eight conditional deposit had been returned and listed security released; the loan balance did not restore the unsupported sale. The former buyer's authorized receiver had already signed the actual refund. Today Han approved the practical property comparison for the posted copy. He asked that it name his valid claim as plainly as the title limit. Tian agreed, and neither pretended the agreement made them friends.

canal_p22_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_068.text: The repaired return map remained on the board with the damaged portion visibly closed and the sound winter alternative shown. Its separate estimate request had an actual receiving number at the ordinary route office. The cabinet maker's private shed permission and next-month rent amendment remained in their own files. Temporary storage could not erase the common line from a working copy again. Yue gave the tenant the final practical notice he had requested. He read it beside a finished table leg and said he could work around an inconvenient line better than a mysterious one.

canal_p22_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_069.text: Bao's accepted pay and the emergency injury transfer did not change because he was absent from the second morning. His clinician's current loaded-work restriction remained, with brief light observation permitted. The ordinary closing physical adjustment had been completed by the qualified mason under the quarter-day transfer. Yue placed the actual restriction beside the remaining handover interval. A final ceremony could not authorize a painful demonstration the clinical review had refused. Bao's sister collected his approved work copy, leaving private household details out. She said he was teaching a small drawing lesson and had finally stopped calling sitting a defeat.

canal_p22_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_070.text: The fuel remained in commission custody with the exact selected meter records and a conservative floor of two hundred forty-four units. No pulse had been made during dry receiving, route clearing, or the hearing. Eight stones remained stored, not distributed as rewards. Future powered work would need a funded qualified operator and the measured rated condition. Jiang's completed appointments did not silently extend through winter. Yue checked the receiving sheet and then stopped thinking about the frame for the rest of the interval. It had performed its bounded work; the charter needed people able to leave it waiting.

canal_p22_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_071.text: Yue's cumulative ordinary pay remained twenty, with four due only after the final two equivalents were actually completed. Her personal three-copper ordinary fare was paid, and four copper stayed held for food and beds on the two-day journey. Ren's fifty-ninth morning was actually accepted. Any owed physical orchard visit still waited for Yue's arrival under the retained arrangement. The optional west-kiln connection would cost one additional personal copper if chosen. She checked that final public duties still fitted the fifty-sixth closure rather than asking the appointment to stretch around the town's newest unanswered problem.

canal_p22_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_072.text: Tian had three mornings before the real sail fitting on the fifty-fifth afternoon. The customer and observer had confirmed the interval; the winter trial remained conditional on the practical result and her own choice. She asked her mother to check the sail roll for an ordinary damp patch. The older woman found one and complained, delighted to contribute something useful. Yue watched them spread the cloth on the private rack without turning it into public laundry. The plant on Luo's window sill had survived one practice watering and looked offensively pleased with itself.

canal_p22_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_073.text: The young keeper brought her current round book to Pei. Two small receiving corrections remained, both made from actual replies rather than guessed household duties. The principal and alternate were named, the late warning-conditioned cargo interval was closed unless fresh priced service existed, and the longer winter route was usable under its checked conditions. Luo approved the round without offering to walk it a second time merely to feel needed. Yue saw the girl straighten at the trust. The gatekeeper then asked for her kettle back, establishing that some forms of authority would never be shared peacefully.

canal_p22_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_074.text: The old check worker's contact stayed on the task board. His two-copper private inventory had been earned and paid, while future work remained uncertain. The washing woman's copied contact request stood nearby. The separately funded assistant had actual short intervals and an end date; she would not transform empty offers into jobs. Yue brought the worker the approved chosen wording about reduced recurring checks. He read it outside his house and said the sentence was fair. Fairness would not pay his winter rent, but unfair description would have made another thing harder. He thanked her for the smaller result.

canal_p22_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_075.text: The quarry representative left by the ordinary afternoon boat with the current finding, penalty receipt, and bounded contribution records. The private corrected outlet belonged to future inspections, not Yue's pack. He asked whether she would return next season. She said she had no accepted canal appointment then. The answer seemed to disappoint him; perhaps he had found her a convenient person through whom to speak to the whole town. Luo gave him the actual current receiver contact. A workable handover sometimes began when the visitor stopped being the easiest door to knock on.

canal_p22_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_076.text: Pei and her assistant read the final hearing folder once more, then tied it in its dry cover. They did not read until exhaustion made errors more likely. The hearing had established a permit breach and finite actual payments, carried bounded water findings, and left the charter for final closure approval. The town could dispute those things through named routes without claiming every story remained frozen until Yue solved it personally. She helped place the folder on its broad-labeled shelf. The assistant could find it without knowing the particular angle at which Pei liked to leave a knot.

canal_p22_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_077.text: At supper Luo asked whether a charter could make people kinder. Tian said a good one might at least make unkindness easier to identify. Han's wife, invited for a brief meal after her own work, said kindness also required somebody to peel the turnips. Yue took the knife with her ordinary sound hands and peeled badly enough to lose an unnecessary strip. Tian rescued the next turnip. Their conversation moved from money to food to the proposed sail trial. The document on the office board did not need to contain this meal for the meal to matter.

canal_p22_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p22_078.text: The fifty-third night was quiet. The ordinary gate kept its level, the damaged old step and return edge stayed closed, and the source papers rested with their actual holders. Yue laid out the last closing task list beside Ren's accepted date. Two days remained before Tian's fitting, three before canal closure, and six before the physical orchard review. She would finish what she had actually accepted without pretending the town had no future losses. Outside, someone laughed by the landing. The sound traveled a long way across water that belonged to no single listener.
